rules.title: Server Version in Header
rules.hint: Version banners let attackers match the server against known CVEs

rules.title: Operating System in Server Header
rules.hint: Operating system and distribution details narrow down exploitable packages and kernel issues

rules.title: Server Modules and Versions in Header
rules.hint: Module and library versions in the banner can be matched against known vulnerabilities

rules.title: {header} Header
rules.hint: Technology and version headers fingerprint the backend stack

rules.title: Debug Header Exposed
rules.hint: Debug tokens and profiler links can expose request internals; check the linked profiler endpoint

rules.title: Source File Paths Exposed in Header
rules.hint: Visual Studio Browser Link header discloses encoded server-side source file paths; the site is running in debug mode

rules.title: Backend Server Identity Header
rules.hint: Backend hostnames reveal infrastructure layout and can aid targeting of origin servers

rules.title: Client or Proxy IP Header in Response
rules.hint: Echoed IP headers indicate how the proxy chain trusts client-supplied addresses; test IP-based access controls for spoofing

rules.title: Proxy Chain Disclosed in Via Header
rules.hint: Via reveals intermediate proxies, cache software and sometimes versions or internal hostnames

rules.title: {header} Infrastructure Header
rules.hint: Infrastructure headers reveal the CDN, cloud provider or proxy layers in front of the application

rules.title: Server-Timing Header Exposes Internals
rules.hint: Timing metrics can reveal backend components, database calls and processing stages

rules.title: ETag Reveals File Inode
rules.hint: Apache-style inode-size-mtime ETags leak file system inode numbers and modification times

rules.title: Source Map Header
rules.hint: Source maps expose original source code, comments and internal paths

rules.title: Internal IP in Response Header
rules.hint: Internal addressing reveals network layout and backend hosts

rules.title: Private IPv6 Address in Response Header
rules.hint: Internal addressing reveals network layout and backend hosts

rules.title: Internal Hostname in Response Header
rules.hint: Internal hostnames reveal naming conventions and reachable backends for SSRF or lateral movement

rules.title: Server File Path in Response Header
rules.hint: File system paths reveal deployment layout and usernames

rules.title: Credentials in URL Within Header
rules.hint: A URL with embedded username and password is exposed in a response header; treat the credentials as compromised
rules.evidence: {header} contains a URL with embedded credentials

rules.title: AWS Access Key in Response Header
rules.hint: Credentials in response headers must be treated as compromised; rotate and verify what they grant
rules.evidence: {header} contains an AWS access key ID

rules.title: JWT in Response Header
rules.hint: Tokens in non-standard headers can be cached or logged by intermediaries; decode it and check claims and lifetime

rules.title: Cache Server Software Header
rules.hint: Caching headers reveal the CDN/cache software and layer in front of the application

rules.title: WAF or Security Proxy Identity Header
rules.hint: WAF identity headers reveal which protection is in front of the application, aiding bypass research

rules.title: WWW-Authenticate Header Exposed
rules.hint: Discloses the authentication scheme and sometimes an internal realm name or server identity

rules.title: {header} Header
rules.hint: Technology and version headers fingerprint the backend stack

rules.title: {header} Reporting Header
rules.hint: Network error logging and reporting headers can disclose internal reporting endpoint URLs
